text:
Sasha (SE): quick sync on the multi-cloud POC — customer wants Private/VPC-style connectivity from their on‑prem via ExpressRoute and AWS Direct Connect into a shared services VPC + azure subscription. main asks: preserve client source IP, minimal egress NATing, and cert/breakout options.
Priya (AE): customer stressed about forensics + logging — they need source IP preserved to their internal WAF and IDS. also asked about pricing for endpoints and cross‑region data egress.
Liam (Customer NetOps): yes — we need to see if we can avoid SNAT so logs show original client IP. currently onprem->expressroute->azure-private-endpoint->redwood private app.
Miguel (NetOps): quick facts: Azure Private Endpoint is an interface endpoint in the customer subnet (uses mAC + private IPs). by default traffic to an app behind an NLB/ALB in cloud can break source IP if there is a load balancer doing proxying or if SNAT happens at the NAT gateway. preservation depends on topology: NLB preserves, ALB (L7) terminates TLS and will not preserve.
Miguel (NetOps): for AWS path: use an NLB + target groups with proxy protocol v2 or preserve client IP in IP target mode. with interface endpoints (AWS VPCE) we can keep private connectivity.
Sasha (SE): tl;dr options: (1) terminate TLS at customer's edge and forward traffic through a TCP NLB to preserve SrcIP, (2) use mutual TLS back to the app (mTLS) so termination can be safe while still surfacing original identity in headers, (3) accept SNAT and rely on X-Forwarded-For + logging.
Anika (Security): security checklist — if we rely on XFF, ensure we control the fronting proxy and have strict header validation; for mTLS we need cert lifecycle across orgs. Also need KMS/HSM integration notes for Private deployment.
Priya (AE): customer also asked about firewall allowlist. can we provide minimal CIDR list or FQDNs? they want something to hand to corporate firewall team.
Miguel (NetOps): we can give two options: static EIP ranges for a dedicated connector (preferred) OR FQDN allowlist for hosted (less strict). sample rules: 
```
# allow outbound to Redwood endpoints
allow tcp 443 to 52.14.200.0/24
allow tcp 443 to 18.204.0.0/16
# if using interface endpoint, allow VPC cidr and peering ranges
allow tcp 443 from 10.10.0.0/16
```
(These are placeholders — will provide exact ranges and per-region lists in follow-up)
Liam (Customer NetOps): we run policy that forbids wildcard FQDNs, so we prefer CIDRs. would dedicated reserved IPs be an option for POC?
Sasha (SE): yes — for Dedicated we can assign static egress IPs (sticky EIP/NAT) so you can hand those to firewall. pricing implication: reserved capacity + static EIP mapping has a monthly cost. I'll pull a quick estimate.
Priya (AE): pls attach the POC quote line item — customer asked for 3 weeks POC, 10k req/day estimate, and 2TB egress. they want cost split host/transfer.
Sasha (SE): noted. I'll run numbers with infra team. Miguel, can you confirm whether an NLB in front of the private app is required to preserve SrcIP in both AWS and Azure topologies?
Miguel (NetOps): AWS: use NLB (L4) with IP targets or enable proxy protocol. Azure: preserve IP if you use VM/VM scale set backend with Instance-Level IP, but Application Gateway (ALB equiv) will terminate TLS and not preserve. For Private Endpoint in Azure we usually present the service on a nic in the VNet — traffic from onprem once routed over ExpressRoute will be 1:1 and not SNATed unless NAT gateway is in path. So topology matters.
Anika (Security): we also need to send customer the security questionnaire answers: certs, SOC2, encryption in transit + at rest, KMS integration. Sasha, can you attach the one‑pager?
Sasha (SE): will attach. also adding notes about DNS: customer must either do DNS zone forwarding to our private zone or create a private DNS link so azure private endpoint resolves to the service IP. if they use split‑horizon DNS we need to coordinate TTLs.
Liam (Customer NetOps): ok — DNS team will do conditional forwarders. whats the recommended TTL?
Sasha (SE): 60s–300s recommended for POC. low TTL during rollout so we can flip targets.
Priya (AE): next steps: 1) Sasha to send CIDR static EIP list + POC cost estimate, 2) Miguel to draw simple topology diagram for AWS+Azure+onprem showing NAT/NLB positions, 3) Anika to answer security questionnaire draft. target: EOD tomorrow to prep for Friday demo.
Miguel (NetOps): I'll post a diagram and call out where SrcIP is preserved vs SNATed.
Sasha (SE): adding note: if customer wants WAF in front, prefer inline NLB + WAF appliance that supports proxy-protocol or pass-through TLS. otherwise ALB will make logs show ALB IP.
Liam (Customer NetOps): thanks — this helps. we'll get firewall ticket ready once you send the EIPs.

Sasha (SE): will do — attaching follow-ups in this thread.
